List the TLS certificates this organization watches, with the newest check beside each one: last_status, days_until_expiry and expires_at. A monitor no check has run against yet answers last_status "unchecked". `discovered` is true for a monitor found by Kubernetes or ACM discovery rather than created by a person, which is the monitor discovery proposes again after a delete. Optionally filter by enabled, or by that flag. Included in the Business and Enterprise plans.

post.description: Watch a hostname's TLS certificate. The platform opens a TLS connection to hostname:port every check_interval_hours, records what it found, and raises an alert once the certificate is within warn_days_before of expiry and a sharper one within critical_days_before. It alerts on a certificate that fails verification too, whatever its expiry date says: an untrusted chain or a wrong-host certificate is already failing for everything that checks one. warn_days_before must be greater than critical_days_before, or a certificate between the two would be announced as the milder of the two problems. A host on a private, loopback or otherwise non-public address is refused, because a monitor is a standing instruction to dial it unattended. The first check runs on the next scheduled check; check_certificate_now runs one at once. Included in the Business and Enterprise plans.

check_interval_hours.description: How often to check, at least 1. Default 24.

critical_days_before.description: Days of validity left that raise the sharper one. Default 7, and it must be below warn_days_before.

hostname.description: The host to connect to, 1 to 253 characters. A wildcard certificate has no host to dial, so name a concrete one.

warn_days_before.description: Days of validity left that raise the first alert. Default 30.

The Slack routing for infrastructure changes (deployments, scaling, pod restarts, config changes, rollbacks): whether it is on, the channel, the event types announced and the namespace filter. Read from the workspace the Settings page's card edits, which is the enabled one, else the first configured. A workspace with nothing stored answers what would be announced if it were switched on.

post.description: Create an infrastructure connector a runbook step can act through. connector_type is one of kubernetes, ssh, aws_ecs, aws_lambda, aws_ec2, aws_eks, aws_iam, aws_cleanup. aws_iam is the IAM hygiene connector and only self-healing's Security area acts through it (no runbook step can use it, and no read of the account does): it reads a user's access keys and changes a key's status, with a role of its own that needs exactly iam:GetAccessKeyLastUsed, iam:GetUser, iam:ListAccessKeys, iam:UpdateAccessKey on the account's users. aws_cleanup is the only role SRE Agent deletes with (IAM access keys and console passwords, unattached volumes, unassociated Elastic IPs, old snapshots and images, and the retention of log groups that never expire): without it nothing is ever deleted, whatever the autonomy tier. Only self-healing's Security and FinOps areas act through it, after an acknowledgement that names deletions; no runbook step can use it and no read of the account does. Its role is its own and needs exactly autoscaling:DescribeLaunchConfigurations, cloudtrail:DescribeTrails, cloudtrail:LookupEvents, ec2:CreateSnapshot, ec2:CreateTags, ec2:CreateVolume, ec2:DeleteSnapshot, ec2:DeleteVolume, ec2:DeregisterImage, ec2:DescribeAddresses, ec2:DescribeAddressesAttribute, ec2:DescribeImageAttribute, ec2:DescribeImages, ec2:DescribeInstances, ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions, ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplates, ec2:DescribeSnapshotAttribute, ec2:DescribeSnapshots, ec2:DescribeVolumes, ec2:ListImagesInRecycleBin, ec2:ListSnapshotsInRecycleBin, ec2:ReleaseAddress, ec2:RestoreImageFromRecycleBin, ec2:RestoreSnapshotFromRecycleBin, iam:DeleteAccessKey, iam:DeleteLoginProfile, iam:GetAccessKeyLastUsed, iam:GetGroupPolicy, iam:GetLoginProfile, iam:GetPolicy, iam:GetPolicyVersion, iam:GetUser, iam:GetUserPolicy, iam:ListAccessKeys, iam:ListAttachedGroupPolicies, iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies, iam:ListGroupPolicies, iam:ListGroupsForUser, iam:ListMFADevices, iam:ListUserPolicies, kms:CreateGrant, kms:Decrypt, kms:DescribeKey, kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext, kms:ReEncryptFrom, kms:ReEncryptTo, logs:DeleteRetentionPolicy, logs:DescribeLogGroups, logs:ListTagsForResource, logs:PutRetentionPolicy, rbin:GetRule, rbin:ListRules, with a Deny of every deletion on resources tagged sre-agent:protect. aws_eks is for discovery: it lists EKS clusters and the workloads Container Insights reports, and like every AWS connector it also reads the account-wide inventory (VPCs, subnets, security groups, load balancers, target groups, RDS, ACM). Its role needs exactly these read grants and nothing that writes: acm:ListCertificates, cloudwatch:ListMetrics, ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups, ec2:DescribeSubnets, ec2:DescribeVpcs, eks:DescribeCluster, eks:ListClusters, elasticloadbalancing:DescribeLoadBalancers, elasticloadbalancing:DescribeTargetGroups, rds:DescribeDBInstances. Runbook actions through it need their own grants. To reach EC2 instances via SSM, use aws_ec2 and grant the AWS credentials ssm:SendCommand. `config` holds the type-specific credentials: kubernetes -> {"kubeconfig":"..."}; ssh -> {"host","user","private_key","port"}; aws_* -> {"auth_type":"aws_assume_role"|"aws_access_keys", "role_arn"|"access_key_id"/"secret_access_key", "region"}. metadata labels drive connector selection when several of a type exist.

get.description: List this organization's data sources: name, type, url, enabled and regions. A source that assumes an AWS role also answers role_arn and aws_account_id (the account segment of that ARN), so sources sharing one role are visible without opening each source. For AWS you may pass regions (a list) instead of url. cloudwatch_metrics, cloudwatch_logs, cloudtrail and xray share one account's role: connecting any one of them is enough for reads of all four, so a second row is only needed for a different account or a precise route. post.description: Escalate the alerts a rule matches to one target, once per firing per alert. A rule with no match_source, match_severity or match_labels matches every alert in the organization. Setting escalate_after_minutes makes it a timed rule instead, which pages for the alerts it matches once their firing has lasted that long; read that field's description before setting it.

cooldown_minutes.description: An immediate rule waits this long, at least 1, after a delivered page before it pages about a DIFFERENT alert; a page the target refused spends nothing, so every matching alert still gets its own attempt and its own row. A timed rule does not space its pages by this at all: one pass of the escalation checker pages for every alert it matches whose firing has lasted long enough, and the number is read only as the seed of the retry wait below. Either kind of rule waits this long before re-attempting a page that could not be delivered, doubling the wait with each further failure up to one day; the immediate path makes that attempt on the next delivery of the alert that arrives after the wait, and the timed path on its next pass. Neither repeats a page that was delivered for the same firing. null leaves the default of 30 minutes.

enabled.description: Whether this rule may fire at all. A disabled rule keeps everything it matches on and is skipped.

escalate_after_minutes.description: Makes this a timed rule, at least 1, and it changes when the rule pages rather than what it pages for. A timed rule is run by the escalation checker, which pages once per firing for the alerts it matches, and only once the firing has lasted this many minutes; an alert that cleared and fired again is firing since the moment it came back, however long it was open before that. match_source, match_severity and match_labels are read the same way as on an immediate rule. A page the target refuses is attempted again at growing intervals, starting at cooldown_minutes after the failure and doubling with each further failure up to one day, and one that was delivered is never repeated for that alert and rule in that firing. null leaves the rule immediate, and an immediate rule pages for the alerts it matches as they arrive: once per firing per alert, so a redelivery of an alert that is still active does not page again and an alert that cleared and fired again does.

match_labels.description: Only alerts whose labels carry every one of these pairs, compared as strings, so every value here must be a string. An empty object and null both match every alert.

get.description: List this organization's per-repository fix settings: each row's id, the branch it applies to (null means all branches), the service alias, the environment, and the write fence (directories and writable extensions, and allow_ci_config, which says whether fixes may change CI configuration inside those directories). Each repository also reports `fix_runner`, which says who executes its fix requests: "platform", SRE Agent's own agent, or "self_hosted", your own machine. Each repository also reports `following`, per setting true when the value is the organization default (get_repository_defaults) and false when the repository's own settings set it. The id is what update_repo_settings and delete_repo_settings address a row by; the runner is set with those tools or by an admin under Integrations, and both check that a runner is registered for your organization before saving "self_hosted". A repository with no settings is not listed (list_effective_repo_settings lists every repository): it is still targetable by a fix request, with an auto-detected fence and the organization default runner, built-in platform when none is set. alerting_sns_topic_arn, when set, is the SNS topic an "Alarm on this" pull request for the repository reuses instead of creating one. auto_dispatch false means the repository waits for a person to press Send on a fix request (on its card, or in the Control Tower) before it is sent; platform_fallback true (the organization default, built-in true) means a request the repository's own runner could not finish may run on SRE Agent's own runner; false keeps the code on your machines and the request fails instead. Each branch row also reports check_network, whether the repository's commands after setup (checks, tests, analysis) may reach GitHub and the package registries while a fix is checked or verified; off unless an admin turned it on (for the repository or as the organization default). It also reports draft_prs, the value in force for that row: whether a fix pull request opens as a draft (true), ready for review (false), or by the installation's setting (null), taken from the row's own choice, else the organization default. `following` says whether the row's own settings set it, so an update that sends the value back makes it the row's own. Each branch row also reports `set_here`, the settings that row holds a value for (the rest follow the default), and update_repo_settings with follows_default puts a setting back on it. ci_fallback_to_platform is stored and has no effect today: nothing reads it.

post.description: Create the settings for one repository the GitHub App can reach: the write fence remediation obeys, an optional service alias, and which runner executes the repository's fix requests. A repository the App does not reach is refused rather than saved, because the fix pipeline would never read the row. Settings are optional: a repository with no row is still targetable, with its fence detected on first use. A setting you do not give is not stored: the row follows the organization default for it (follows_default is accepted as in update_repo_settings: the new row follows anyway, and fix_runner, platform_fallback or auto_dispatch named there are also cleared on the repository's other rows). A branch row takes the runner, the runner fallback and how requests are sent from the repository's other rows. Creating the all-branches row (no branch) of a repository that has branch rows moves none of them: each keeps what it was reading, the value is written onto it, and the answer carries pinned_branches (how many, only when above zero). Answers the repository in the shape list_repo_settings answers.

alerting_sns_topic_arn.description: The SNS topic ARN an "Alarm on this" pull request for this repository should name in a generated alarm's alarm_actions, when one already exists for this repository's AWS account and region. Left unset, that pull request creates its own topic and subscription the first time and reuses it (by name) after that.

allow_ci_config.description: Whether fixes may change CI configuration (.github/, .circleci/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile and similar) inside path_prefixes. Off by default. Each such change opens as a draft pull request that names the CI files and is never merged by SRE Agent, and CI files are never pushed onto a pull request whose auto-merge is on. Name it in follows_default to put this row back on the default. With this on, a fix may change CI configuration, and the repository's CI runs that change as soon as the branch is pushed, with the repository's secrets, before anyone reviews the pull request. Every way a fix starts can make such a change: fix requests, @sre-agent change, automatic investigation and self-healing pull requests, and revise-on-review.

auto_dispatch.description: true (the organization default, built-in true) sends this repository's fix requests to its runner as soon as they are made. false waits for a person: every request, from any source (the webhook included), is created and its card says it is waiting, but nothing is sent until someone presses Send on the card (or, for a request with no card, in its Control Tower drawer). Send follows the organization's fix_request_floor: when it is member, members can send a held request too, so the wait is for anyone who may request fixes, not an org admin's review. Applies to the whole repository; name it in follows_default to put the whole repository back on the organization default.

branch.description: The branch this row applies to. Leave it out (or send null) for the all-branches row, which is what a repository with one fence wants.

check_network.description: Whether the repository's commands after setup (checks, tests, analysis) may reach GitHub and the package registries while a fix is checked or verified. Off by default: setup commands always reach those hosts to install dependencies, and every command after setup reaches no network. On, those commands, and code a fix writes and runs, can send the repository's source or command output to any account on those hosts. Applies to the row it is sent for. Turning it on is accepted only where the Integrations page offers it (code improvement on your plan and check sessions running on the platform); turning it off always is. Name it in follows_default to put this row back on the default.

draft_prs.description: Whether a fix pull request for this repository opens as a draft: true always as a draft, false ready for review, null (the organization default, else the installation's draft_prs setting) as it says. Answers report the value in force (the row's own choice, else the organization default); `following` says whether the row sets it, and sending a value makes it the row's own. When the setting is ready for review, a change the sandbox saw fail, an open self-review blocker or CI configuration files still open as a draft and the pull request says why, and a change the checks could not judge opens ready with a "Not verified" line saying why. Applies to the entry it is sent for. Name it in follows_default (or send null) to put the entry back on the default.

get.description: The organization's repository defaults: the six settings every repository without its own value follows (fix_runner, platform_fallback, auto_dispatch, draft_prs, check_network, allow_ci_config), as one flat object. `source` says where they come from: "own" (this organization set them), "parent" (a child organization follows its parent's), or "built_in" (none set: platform runner, fallback on, automatic dispatch, no network for checks, no CI configuration changes, pull requests by the installation's setting). `inherited_from` is the parent organization's id when the values are the parent's, `parent_name` the parent's name when there is one, and `stopped` is true when a child chose to stop following its parent. Change them with update_repository_defaults; list_effective_repo_settings shows what each repository ends up with.

put.description: Change the organization's repository defaults: the settings a repository follows until it has its own value. An organization admin's tool, the same as the Organization defaults for repositories panel under Integrations. Send the settings to change, or follow_parent true (a child organization goes back to its parent's defaults and drops its own), or stop_following true (a child stops following its parent and uses the built-in values); send only one of those three kinds. The preview lists the change, the repositories that would move, how many keep a value of their own, a count per following child organization, the confirmations needed (needs_confirm) and anything that refuses it, with a fingerprint. Over this API a write takes two requests. Send the change: the answer is 428 with the preview in preview and its fingerprint at preview.data.fingerprint, and nothing is written. Send the same body with expected_fingerprint set to that fingerprint to apply it (200). If what would move changed since the preview, nothing is written and the answer is 409 with a fresh preview. Turning allow_ci_config or check_network on needs confirm ["ci_config"] or ["check_network"] when applying. A child organization that follows its parent and sends only some of the six settings starts its own defaults from the parent's current values for the rest and stops following the parent for all six; the preview says so with leaves_parent true, and follow_parent undoes it. An API key with mcp:admin (api:admin on the configuration API) may use every part of it, follow_parent and stop_following included. An applied change leaves one repository_defaults.changed audit entry. This changes what repositories follow; update_repo_settings writes a repository's own value (or puts it back on the default with follows_default), and set_platform_fallback_for_all sets the runner fallback default and makes every repository follow it.

allow_ci_config.description: Whether fixes may change CI configuration inside the write fence of following repositories. Turning it on needs confirm ci_config. With this on, a fix may change CI configuration, and the repository's CI runs that change as soon as the branch is pushed, with the repository's secrets, before anyone reviews the pull request. Every way a fix starts can make such a change: fix requests, @sre-agent change, automatic investigation and self-healing pull requests, and revise-on-review.

auto_dispatch.description: true sends a following repository's fix requests as soon as they are made. false holds each until a person presses Send.

check_network.description: Whether the commands after setup (checks, tests, analysis) of following repositories may reach GitHub and the package registries while a fix is checked. Turning it on needs confirm check_network and is accepted only where the Integrations page offers it.

confirm.description: The confirmations the change needs, from needs_confirm in the preview: ci_config for allow_ci_config true, check_network for check_network true.

draft_prs.description: Whether a following repository's fix pull request opens as a draft (true), ready for review (false), or by the installation's setting (null).

expected_fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the preview you reviewed; required to write. With apply, a fingerprint that no longer matches writes nothing and answers the fresh preview. A blank or non-string value is refused.

fix_runner.description: Who executes the fix requests of repositories that follow: platform, self_hosted. "self_hosted" needs a runner registered for this organization. Included in the Business and Enterprise plans.

follow_parent.description: true: a child organization drops its own defaults and follows its parent's again. Not combined with settings or stop_following.

platform_fallback.description: true lets a request a following repository's own runner could not finish run on SRE Agent's own runner. false keeps the code on your machines: the request fails with a plain sentence instead.

stop_following.description: true: a child organization stops following its parent and uses the built-in values. Not combined with settings or follow_parent.

get.description: The organization's request signing: its key ids with their state (signing, pending, verify_only, retired, revoked) and times, the hosts its configuration sends requests to with whether each is signed, remote_locations_pending (true while a check that runs from a remote location has not yet had its signature confirmed, so a signed host may still be reached unsigned from there), the SRE-Agent-Signature header format and the address of the verification guide. Never a key: the key is revealed on Settings, Request signing, by an organization admin. Admin floor, like the page. Every plan.

The allow rules for credentials found in repositories, oldest first, at most 100: id, repository (null for every repository), path_glob, detector_type (null for every kind), reason, expires_at (null for never) and created_at. The weekly scan files nothing for a match a rule covers; a rule closes nothing already filed. Included in the Business and Enterprise plans.

At most 100 rules. A rule closes nothing already filed. Organization admin floor. Included in the Business and Enterprise plans.

get.description: One tracker's import rule by provider, the same fields list_ticket_import_rules answers for it. Refused when that tracker has no rule.

put.description: Say which of a tracker's issues become cards on their own, one standing rule per tracker. An issue the rule names gets a card in Triage with its tracker item already linked, so a team that files in their own tracker still sees the work on the board. Saving a rule imports nothing by itself: it decides what arrives from here on, and run_ticket_import fetches what is already open. Jira and Zoho Sprints need their credentials saved first (configure_ticket_integration); GitHub needs none, because it goes through the App installation this organization already connected.

config.description: What to import, in this tracker's own terms: github: repo, label; jira: project, label; zoho_sprints: project, item_type. The repository is owner/name, the projects are the tracker's own key or id, and a label or item type narrows the rule to issues carrying it. Rebuilt whole on every call: a key left out is dropped and {} clears it. Every value is a non-blank string, and a key this tracker does not have is refused by name.

enabled.description: Whether matching issues become cards. Switched off, the rule is kept and nothing is imported, which is how an import is stopped without losing what it names.

get.description: The ticket systems this organization writes into, as the Integrations page's Tickets tab lists them: the provider (zoho_sprints, jira), whether it is enabled, the API host, the board columns mapped onto its workflow, and where a new item would be filed. No credential is ever returned: client_secret_set, refresh_token_set and api_token_set say only whether one is stored, and create_ready says whether the destination is complete enough to file an item rather than only comment on one.

post.description: Save this organization's credentials for one ticket system, one row per provider. Zoho Sprints authenticates with client_id, client_secret and refresh_token against auth_url; Jira with account_email and api_token. Only the fields you send change, an omitted secret keeps the stored one, and the board columns are mapped with set_ticket_status_map rather than here.

account_email.description: Jira only: the account the API token belongs to, as an email address.

api_token.description: Jira only: the API token that account authenticates with. Replaced and refused on the same terms as client_secret.

auth_url.description: Zoho Sprints only: the accounts server its access tokens are minted at, which is a different host from the API.

auto_file.description: File every card created from now on into this system without a button press; later edits sync on their own. Needs a destination (project_key, or all three Zoho ids). Cards that already exist are never filed by this.

base_url.description: Where the API lives, per customer rather than a constant: Zoho serves seven data centres on seven domains and every Jira is its own host. Required the first time a provider is saved.

client_id.description: Zoho Sprints only: the self-client's id from the Zoho API console.

client_secret.description: Zoho Sprints only: the self-client's secret. Sending it replaces whatever is stored; an empty one is refused rather than read as a way to remove it.

create_project_id.description: Zoho Sprints only: the project a new item is filed into.

create_sprint_id.description: Zoho Sprints only: the sprint a new item is filed into.

create_team_id.description: Zoho Sprints only: the team a new item is filed into. Zoho addresses an item by three ids, so all three are needed to create one, or none of them.

enabled.description: Whether the platform may write into this system. Switched off, the credentials are kept and nothing is sent.

issue_type.description: Jira only: the issue type a new issue is filed as, for example Task.

project_key.description: Jira only: the project a new issue is filed into. Without it this connection can comment on an issue and not open one.

provider.description: Which ticket system, one of: zoho_sprints, jira. One connection each.

refresh_token.description: Zoho Sprints only: the long-lived token an access token is swapped for on every call. Replaced and refused on the same terms as client_secret.

delete.description: Remove this organization's credentials for one ticket system, with the board column mapping and the create destination stored beside them. Cards already linked to an item keep their link and stop syncing, and nothing is changed in the ticket system itself. Saving the integration again does not resume them: each card must be unlinked and linked again. This includes the cards of child organizations that file through this integration. To change credentials, save over the existing integration with configure_ticket_integration; to stop writing into it without giving up the credentials, send enabled: false to configure_ticket_integration instead. Needs confirm: true.
